messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @eng-oncall — high error rate and latency spike on continuous-batcher pool us-east-2. Alert: GPU OOMs and container restarts reported (auto-escalation to P0).

alex: I'm on it, grabbing logs and looking at cluster state. p99 latency jumped to ~12s, error rate ~7% for generation routes.

maya: seeing repeated `CUDA error: out of memory` in pod runtime-batcher-7c9f8. Container exit code 137 followed by immediate restart loop.

li: also noticing KV prefetch queue length steadily growing on that node — backlog ~18k entries. That correlates with batch growth on the continuous batcher.

sam: reproducer theory: a prefetch race + aggressive batching causes the batch accumulator to keep growing and never flush because some requests are stuck on slow KV hits. Eventually GPU memory spikes and OOM.

beth: support: two enterprise customers reported 5xxs and slow responses starting ~T-5m. One customer has critical jobs timing out. We need to indicate customer impact ASAP.

alex: quick mitigation plan: 1) move traffic away from affected pool (route to fallback model variant in eu/other region), 2) disable KV prefetch for continuous-batcher on the node, 3) scale up ephemeral capacity for short term.

maya: agree. I'll push a temp config to disable prefetch on the pool. Patch: `ci/disable-kv-prefetch-2468` (will be applied via runtime-configs).

sam: adding hard cap on batch size and queue depth via runtime flags to prevent runaway growth: `--max-batch-size=64 --max-queue-length=2000` — we should apply on the node immediately.

alex: li, can you cordon the node and drain affected pods after traffic cutover? We want a clean restart.

li: cordon + drain in progress. Command used:
```
kubectl cordon gpunode-12-us-east-2
kubectl drain gpunode-12-us-east-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

deploybot: Deploy triggered by maya: runtime-config update `ci/disable-kv-prefetch-2468` -> canary on pool us-east-2, rollout id 8932.

alex: traffic reroute to fallback model variant applied via routing policy. Monitoring now — error rate should drop within one routing window (~30s).

beth: customer comms: sending initial notification to impacted customers, ETA on mitigation 10-15m.

maya: config applied to batcher: prefetch disabled and batch caps set. Logs show queued entries shrinking.

sam: good sign — GPU memory usage on the drained node peaked and is coming down post-drain. No further OOMs in last 45s.

li: node restarted, kernel logs show OOM killer targeted process `runtime-batcher` before container exit. We've opened a kernel-level trace for follow up.

alex: can we do a live patch to the accumulator to ensure stuck requests get a timeout? We need an immediate short-term guard.

maya: pushing hotspot fix that sets a soft timeout of 6s on KV lookups and will force batch flush if any entry exceeds that. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/5943 (hotfix branch `hotfix/kv-timeouts`).

deploybot: Hotfix PR queued, requesting manual approval for emergency deploy.

sam: approving from runtime side. Note: this is temporary, will introduce slightly higher tail errors for slow KV but prevents runaway memory usage.

alex: approved, deploying hotfix to canary subset now.

incident-bot: Incident timeline updated. Severity escalated -> P0. Oncall owners: alex (incident lead), maya (runtime), li (sre).

beth: customers updated: one customer paused jobs to avoid timeouts, another switched to fallback region. Keeping them informed.

maya: hotfix rolling, canary looks stable. p95 latency back down from 5.8s to 1.2s on rerouted traffic.

sam: monitoring: no more OOMs in the last 4 minutes across the cluster. Batch queue lengths normalized.

li: post-mortem notes: root cause appears to be a combination of unbounded prefetch + no timeout on pending KV requests causing batch accumulators to wait indefinitely and grow. We'll need a longer-term fix: 1) make prefetch adaptive, 2) backpressure from KV layer, 3) stronger integration tests for queue-starvation scenarios.

alex: handoff plan: I'm oncall for another 15m, will update incident board and then hand over to li for post-incident follow-up and paging rule adjustments.

beth: I'll draft customer incident summary and share in #customer-incidents after the handoff.

li: taking post-incident ownership after alex. I'll coordinate rollback vs permanent patch decisions with runtime and SRE.

alex: thanks everyone. Marking incident as mitigated for active customer impact. Keeping P0 open until hotfix is in prod and root-cause PRs are scheduled. :thumbsup:

maya: created tickets: INC-4621 (hotfix deployed), ENG-9142 (long-term batching fixes), SRE-377 (routing policy test coverage).

deploybot: Hotfix rollout completed: 100% on us-east-2 pool.

li: closing loop — no further restarts seen in last 10m. I'll start the postmortem doc and invite runtime + SRE.

beth: customer follow-ups scheduled.

alex: handing off to li now. Good job team.

li: received handoff. Will continue with post-incident analysis and timeline writeup.

incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Assigned owner: li.
